editorial_findings: The strongest defensible tension is supported: energy dominated the goods increase while services and the explicitly defined underlying measure also rose. The 80% attribution remains confined to goods, never total final demand.
All reviewed headline/component values match the bound source records: headline 1.3, goods 2.6, services 0.8, underlying 0.5; nested rates 1.2/10.8/0.3 and 1.4/3.4/0.3 percent monthly SA.

The 24-month chart retains first-release values and the prose explicitly distinguishes the September-release revised July/August comparators. No post-event observation, current-vintage replacement or record-high claim was introduced.

The article contains a substantive concentration/volatility countercase and a conditional future test. It does not convert this producer-price release into an automatic CPI or Federal Reserve forecast.

Canonical photo credit is complete and accessible: Chris, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0, with exact UK/16 June 2017 archive context. The unchanged photograph is modestly displayed and not treated as price/event evidence.

All nine local reading views preserve the dated retrospective framing and Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade. Native payload previews do not strengthen the article claims.

The three rendered charts are complete and unclipped. At mobile width the images are thumbnails with full-size links; surrounding prose and captions preserve the essential numbers, dates, definitions and uncertainty.
The local review shell retains status/source disclosures. Those controls are distinct from the authored article body and are not publication evidence.
